page: Hetzner Cloud cpx41 is a regular-purpose cloud server powered by the AMD EPYC processor family on the x86_64 architecture, managed via the QEMU hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 8 shared vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, coupled with 16 GB of system memory, providing 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside standard x86 instruction extensions including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, while lacking AVX-512 or AMX accelerators. Local persistent storage is bundled with a 240 GB NVMe SSD, though no dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark evaluations place the cpx41 firmly in the middle performance tier across multi-threaded computational workloads. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 7734.0, a PassMark CPU score of 16713.01, and delivers 15.11 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Its memory subsystem registers uncached read bandwidth of 97.09 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 61.62 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing represents a distinct bottleneck; stress-ng single-core performance registers in the lower 10 percent, while gzip single-threaded compression and medium-sized LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker relative throughput.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, cpx41 provides high vCPU and NVMe storage density relative to its hardware class. Because the 8 vCPUs operate on a shared resource model, performance may vary under noisy neighbor conditions. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes parallel thread capacity over per-core memory allocation, making it an economical option for compute tasks that do not demand dedicated core pinning. The configuration aligns well with multi-process web serving, automated CI/CD software compilation, parallel integration testing, containerized microservices, and staging databases.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx41 is a regular-purpose virtual server configured with 8 shared vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture clocked at 2.0 GHz, 16 GB of system RAM, and 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Designed for cost-sensitive environments that benefit from parallel execution across multiple cores, cpx41 maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-threaded processing with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7734.0, a PassMark CPU score of 16713.01, and Redis throughput of 15.11 million operations per second. However, single-core execution is constrained, evidenced by lower stress-ng single-threaded scores. Given its shared CPU allocation model and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, cpx41 provides high multi-core density at an economical hardware profile. It is well matched for scalable web serving, software build environments, staging systems, and microservices where occasional resource contention is tolerable.
